records.source: לְדָוִ֗ד מִ֫זְמ֥וֹרחֶֽסֶד־וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט אָשִׁ֑ירָה לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֲזַמֵּֽרָה׃
records.gloss: Of David. A psalm. Loyal love and justice I will sing; to you, YHWH, I will make music.
pieces: Of David. A psalm. Loyal love and justice will be my song; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will make music for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.1: Of David. A psalm. Of loyal love and justice I will sing; to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will make music.

R.1: By David. A song. I will sing about faithful love and about doing what is fair. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I will make music for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a king's promise
decisions.reason: In this psalm the speaker has a house where others serve him (verses 6-7) and puts the wicked out of the land and out of "the city of the LORD" (verse 8): he speaks as a king, setting out how he will rule. The title links it with David.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: loyal love and justice: what God shows and what the king will practice
decisions.reason: The psalm does not say whose loyal love and justice they are. They are God's (89:15), and they are also what the king vows to practice in the rest of the psalm; both may be meant.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

decisions.choice: By David.
decisions.reason: As in 11:1 and 3:1.

records.heading: A king's vow of integrity

records.source: אַשְׂכִּ֤ילָה׀בְּדֶ֬רֶךְ תָּמִ֗ים מָ֭תַי תָּב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑י אֶתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בְּתָם־לְ֝בָבִ֗י בְּקֶ֣רֶב בֵּיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: I will give heed to [the] way [that is] blameless. When will you come to me? I will walk about in [the] integrity of my heart within my house.
pieces: I will take care to keep to the blameless way. When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to me? Inside my own house I will live with an undivided heart.

L.2: I will give heed to the way [that is] blameless. When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to me? I will walk in the integrity of my heart within my house.

R.2: I will be wise and live a life without fault. When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to be with me? At home, too, I will be honest in all I do.

decisions.choice: give heed: act wisely, pay attention
decisions.reason: The verb (sakal) means to pay attention and so to act with insight. Here the king sets his mind on a blameless life.

decisions.choice: When will you come to me?: a longing for God
decisions.reason: The short question breaks into the vow. Most likely the king longs for God to come to him and bless him, as God promised to come where his name is honored (Exodus 20:24). The words are short and the sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: integrity of heart within my house: honest in private as well
decisions.reason: Integrity (tom) is wholeness with no double dealing (26:1). "Within my house" is the king's own household: his life at home is to match his public vow.

decisions.choice: be honest in all I do
alternatives: walk in the integrity of my heart
decisions.reason: Readable says what walking with a whole heart means.

records.source: לֹֽא־אָשִׁ֨ית׀לְנֶ֥גֶד עֵינַ֗י דְּֽבַר־בְּלִ֫יָּ֥עַל עֲשֹֽׂה־סֵטִ֥ים שָׂנֵ֑אתִי לֹ֖א יִדְבַּ֣ק בִּֽי׃
records.gloss: I will not set before my eyes a thing of worthlessness; [the] doing of [those who] turn aside I hate; it will not cling to me.
pieces: I will not fix my eyes on anything vile. I hate the deeds of those who turn away; they will get no hold on me.

L.3: I will not set before my eyes a worthless thing; the doing of [those who] turn aside I hate; it will not cling to me.

R.3: I will not look with pleasure at anything evil. I hate what people do when they turn away from God. I will not let it stick to me.

decisions.choice: a worthless thing: anything base or wicked
decisions.reason: The word (beliyya'al) means worthlessness and wickedness; "a thing of beliyya'al" can be a wicked deed or a wicked plan (41:9).

decisions.choice: set before my eyes: look at with approval
decisions.reason: To set something before one's eyes is to keep it in view as a goal or delight. The king will not make anything vile his aim.

decisions.choice: the doing of those who turn aside
decisions.reason: The word (setim) occurs only here. It comes from a verb meaning to turn aside, so it is either people who swerve from the right way or the swerving deeds themselves.

decisions.choice: turn away from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what they turn away from (m3).

records.source: לֵבָ֣ב עִ֭קֵּשׁ יָס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נִּי רָ֝֗ע לֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃
records.gloss: A heart perverse will depart from me; evil I will not know.
pieces: A crooked heart will stay far from me; I will not keep company with evil.

L.4: A perverse heart will depart from me; evil I will not know.

R.4: Crooked thinking will stay far away from me. I will not get mixed up in evil.

decisions.choice: a perverse heart: a twisted mind
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the king's own heart (he will not let it become twisted) or people with twisted hearts, whom he will send away. Both fit the vow.

decisions.choice: know: have to do with
decisions.reason: To know (yada') here is to have dealings with, to be on close terms with. The king will have nothing to do with evil.

records.source: מְלָשְׁנִ֬י בַסֵּ֨תֶר׀רֵעֵהוּ֮ אוֹת֪וֹ אַ֫צְמִ֥ית גְּֽבַהּ־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַ֣ב לֵבָ֑ב אֹ֝ת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל׃
records.gloss: [One who] slanders in secret his neighbor, him I will destroy; [one] haughty of eyes and wide of heart, him I will not endure.
pieces: Anyone who secretly slanders a neighbor I will destroy; anyone with lofty eyes and a swollen heart I will not put up with.

L.5: [Whoever] slanders {{gender:their|his}} neighbor in secret, {{gender:that one|him}} I will destroy; [one with] haughty eyes and a proud heart, {{gender:that one|him}} I will not endure.

R.5: If someone secretly tells lies about a neighbor, I will put an end to that person. I will not put up with people who are proud and look down on others.

decisions.choice: slanders: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew text writes the word with a different spelling and its notes say how to read it. The meaning is the same. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: destroy: put an end to
decisions.reason: The verb (tsamat) means to put an end to, to destroy (18:41; 54:7). A king speaks: he will remove such people by his judgment.

decisions.choice: haughty eyes and a wide heart: pride
decisions.reason: High eyes look down on others (18:28); a wide heart is a swollen, arrogant mind (Proverbs 21:4).

decisions.choice: their, that one (with "his", "him" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The words describe anyone who slanders or is proud, so Literal gives inclusive wording by default with the traditional words as the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "anyone" and "people".

records.source: עֵינַ֤י׀בְּנֶֽאֶמְנֵי־אֶרֶץ֮ לָשֶׁ֪בֶת עִמָּ֫דִ֥י הֹ֭לֵךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ תָּמִ֑ים ה֝֗וּא יְשָׁרְתֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: My eyes [are] on [the] faithful of [the] land, to dwell with me; [one who] walks in a way blameless, he will serve me.
pieces: I will watch for those in the land who are faithful and bring them to live with me; those who walk the blameless way will be my servants.

L.6: My eyes [are] on the faithful of the land, to dwell with me; [whoever] walks in a blameless way, {{gender:that one|he}} will serve me.

R.6: I will look for people in the land who can be trusted, and I will keep them near me. Only people who live without fault will work for me.

decisions.choice: my eyes are on: I will look with favor on
decisions.reason: Eyes set on someone mean care and favor (33:18; 34:16). The king will look for faithful people and choose them.

decisions.choice: dwell with me, serve me: the king's court
decisions.reason: The faithful will live at the king's court; the verb serve (sharat) is used of officials in a king's service and of priests serving God.

decisions.choice: that one (with "he" as the alternative)
decisions.reason: As in 101:5.

records.source: לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֨ב׀בְּקֶ֥רֶב בֵּיתִי֮ עֹשֵׂ֪ה רְמִ֫יָּ֥ה דֹּבֵ֥ר שְׁקָרִ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝כּ֗וֹן לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: He will not dwell in [the] midst of my house, [one who] practices deceit; [one who] speaks lies will not be established before my eyes.
pieces: Deceivers will find no home in my house; liars will not keep their place in my sight.

L.7: There will not dwell within my house [one who] practices deceit; [one who] speaks lies will not stand firm before my eyes.

R.7: People who cheat others will not live in my palace. People who tell lies will not stay in my service.

decisions.choice: will not be established before my eyes: will not last in my presence
decisions.reason: To be established (kun) is to stand firm and last. A liar will not keep a place before the king, among those who serve him (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Deceivers, liars (B); People who cheat, people who tell lies (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plural nouns for the singular "one who" of the Hebrew, which means anyone of this kind.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: The king's house is his palace and household (m1 on 101:1).

records.source: לַבְּקָרִ֗ים אַצְמִ֥ית כָּל־רִשְׁעֵי־אָ֑רֶץ לְהַכְרִ֥ית מֵֽעִיר־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: In the mornings I will destroy all [the] wicked of [the] land, to cut off from [the] city of YHWH all doers of wickedness.
pieces: Each morning I will make an end of the wicked in the land, and rid the city of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of all who do wrong.

L.8: Morning by morning I will destroy all the wicked of the land, to cut off from the city of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all [the] doers of wickedness.

R.8: Every morning I will judge cases and put an end to the wicked in the land. I will remove from the city of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} everyone who does evil.

decisions.choice: in the mornings: when the king held court
decisions.reason: The morning was the time for judging cases (Jeremiah 21:12). Each day the king will deal with wrongdoers in his courts.

decisions.choice: the city of the LORD: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem is called the city of the LORD and the city of God (46:5; 48:2, 9). The king's justice is to keep God's city clean.

decisions.choice: the king's justice, not private revenge
decisions.reason: The king speaks of the justice he must do as ruler, under God (72:1-4), not of personal vengeance.

decisions.choice: judge cases
decisions.reason: Readable says what the king does each morning (m1).
